title: INVITE GRATITUDE TO REPLACE COMPLAINT THROUGHOUT THE DAY
text: Lift your hands wherever you are. Just lift your hands to the father. Father, we bless your name. We thank you for this moment, for this gathering of hearts before your throne. Lord, let every word [music] spoken today carry the weight of heaven. Let it pierce the deepest chambers of the human heart. Let it not return to you [music] void. Speak, Lord, for your servants are listening. In Jesus name we pray. Amen. Amen. You may be seated. I want you to open your mouth right now and just begin to [music] bless the Lord. Just begin to say thank you to him. Not because everything is perfect, not because every situation has resolved itself the way you wanted it to, but because [music] he is God. And that alone is enough reason to open your mouth and release gratitude into the atmosphere. Come on, bless his name. Bless him. Bless the Lord, oh my soul. And all that is within me, bless his holy name. Now, I want you to receive this word today with an open spirit. I need you to understand that what I'm about to share with you is not just a motivational thought. It is not a self-help strategy. It is not a psychological tip. What I am about to minister to you today comes from the ancient wells [music] of scripture, from the throne room of the living God and from the deep urgency that the Holy Spirit has placed in my spirit concerning this generation. The Holy Spirit has been troubling me about this. He has been pressing this into my heart because he sees what a generation that has lost the posture of gratitude is becoming and he is not pleased. I want to preach to you today on something that sounds simple but carries the weight of the eternal. I want to speak to you about inviting gratitude to replace complaints throughout the day. I said inviting gratitude, not forcing it, not manufacturing it, but creating the conditions of the heart where gratitude can come in and displace the darkness that complaining produces. And I promise you, by the time you leave this place today, something will shift in your spirit. Something will be healed. Some stronghold [music] will come down and you will never approach your day the same way again. Let me take you to Philippians chapter 4 verse 6. The Apostle Paul writes and says, "Be careful for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God." Now, I want you to see something here. The Apostle Paul was not writing from a luxury hotel. He was not writing from a place of comfort, of ease, of abundance. He was writing from a prison cell. [music] He was writing with chains on his wrists. He was writing from a place of uncertainty where he did not know whether the next thing that would come through the door would be a meal or an execution order. And yet he says be careful for nothing. Do not be anxious for anything. And in the same breath he says with thanksgiving. He ties the discipline of making your requests known to God directly to the posture of thanksgiving. Which means Paul understood something that this generation desperately needs to learn. that you cannot access the full measure of the power of prayer without the vehicle of gratitude. That thanksgiving is not an add-on. It is not the bow on top of the package. It is the very atmosphere in which genuine [music] communion with God becomes possible. Now look at what happens in verse 7. It says, "And the peace of God [music] which passes all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." I need you to see that peace. The peace that surpasses human logic, human reason, human analysis. That kind of peace does not come to people who are constantly rehearsing their problems. That peace is a product of the atmosphere that gratitude creates. When you shift from complain to gratitude, you are not simply changing your mood. You are literally changing the spiritual environment around your life. You are inviting a different frequency. You are opening a different gate. And that gate allows [music] the peace of God to stand guard over your mind like a soldier at the entrance of a palace. This is why the enemy works so hard to keep you in a posture of complaining. You see, the devil is not as creative as people think. He uses the same weapons over and over again. He used them in the Garden of Eden. He used them in the wilderness with Israel. He used them against Job. And he's using them today. And one of his oldest, most effective, most devastating weapons is this. He makes you focus on what you do not have while being blind to what you already possess. He makes you see the gap between where you are and where you want to be. And he magnifies that gap until it becomes the entire landscape of your inner world. And when the gap becomes your entire landscape, complaint becomes the language of your daily life. Listen to me carefully. Complaining is not neutral. I want somebody to hear this because we have been treating complaint like it is harmless venting like it is just expressing yourself like it is just being honest. But beloved, complaining in the biblical context is a form of rebellion against the sovereignty of God. I did not say that Moses said it when Israel was in the wilderness and they murmured against God. Numbers 11 says the anger of the Lord was kindled greatly and God said to Moses, "Why are these people weeping before me? Their complaint was not just an emotional expression. It was a theological statement. It was them saying, "God, what you have given us is not enough. What you have done for us is insufficient. Your provision is inadequate. Your wisdom is questionable. Your love is suspect." Do you understand now why complaint is [music] so dangerous? Because embedded in every complaint is an accusation against the character and the competence of God. I need somebody to feel this. Every time you wake up in the morning and the first words out of your mouth are about what is [music] wrong with your life, you are making a statement about who you believe God is. Every time you spend your evening rehearsing your problems to everyone who will listen, you are building an altar to insufficiency. You are telling the atmosphere around you that the God you serve is not big enough, not wise enough, not loving enough to handle what you are going through. And beloved, that is not just a bad habit. That is a dangerous spiritual posture. But I want to be balanced here because I am not a preacher who ignores the reality of pain. I'm not standing here telling you that your challenges are not real. I am not dismissing the sleepless nights. I am not minimizing the financial pressure. I am not pretending that the broken relationship did not happen, that the medical report was not frightening, that the betrayal did not cut deep. I know it did. I know the pain is real. I know the weight is heavy. But even in the midst of all of that, God is asking you to make a choice about your posture. And that choice will determine everything about what comes next in your life. First Thessalonians 5:18 says this, "In everything give thanks, for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you." I want to draw your attention to a very precise word in that verse. It does not say give thanks [music] for everything. It says give thanks in everything. There is a difference and that difference is everything. God is not asking you to call the cancer good. God is not asking you to celebrate the betrayal. God is not asking you to pretend the loss did not happen. He's asking you to find him in the midst of it. He's asking you to maintain a tether of gratitude to his nature and his goodness even when the circumstances are dark because there is always always always something to be grateful for. Always. Let me show you how gratitude operates as a spiritual technology. When you open your mouth and release thanksgiving, something happens in the realm of the spirit that your natural eyes cannot perceive. Psalm 22:3 says that God inhabits the praises of his people. The Hebrew word there is yashab, which means to dwell, to sit and throne, to settle in. When you praise God, when you thank God, when gratitude flows from your lips like a river, you are essentially building a throne for the King of Kings to sit down upon in the middle of your situation. And when the king sits down in the middle of your situation, the dynamics of that situation must change because [music] a king does not sit in the midst of defeat. A king sits in the midst of dominion. This is what happened with Paul and Silas in Acts 16. They were in a prison. Both their backs were bleeding from the beating they had received. Their feet were locked in stalks. They were in the inner prison, the deepest, darkest, [music] most hopeless part of the facility. And the scripture says that at midnight, Paul and Silas prayed and sang praises unto God. And the prisoners heard them. Now notice what happened next. Suddenly there was a great earthquake so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. And immediately all the doors were opened and everyone's bands were loosed. I need you to see the sequence. Praise goes up, God comes down, [music] and the prison shakes. Gratitude to God in the darkness of midnight did what no lawyer could do, what no petition could accomplish, what no human strategy could engineer. It released a frequency that made earthquakes come and set the captives free. And I'm telling you today that there are situations in your life that have been waiting for you to shift from complaint to [music] gratitude before they can break open. There are doors that will not open to the sound of your murmmory. There are chains that will not fall to the music of your complaints, but they will break when you open your mouth in the midnight season of your life and begin to bless the Lord anyway. I said begin to bless the Lord anyway. Now, let me talk to you about the practice because it is one thing to receive this principle intellectually and another thing entirely to make it the architecture of your daily life. The message today is not just about theology. It is about application. It is about the actual lived experience of waking up on a Tuesday morning when everything in your natural mind wants to rehearse the problems and making the deliberate conscious spirit empowered decision to begin differently to begin with gratitude. The psalmist David understood this in Psalm 59. David was in one of the most dangerous moments of his life. Saul had sent men to watch his house to kill him. His enemies were outside his door. And I want you to see how this man opened his psalm. He starts by crying out to God about the danger. But then he writes something extraordinary. He says, "But I will sing of thy power." Yes, I will sing aloud of thy mercy in the morning. For thou has been my defense and refuge in the day of my trouble. Notice the tension. He was writing in crisis, but he made a declaration about what he would do in the morning. He decided in advance that the morning would begin with song, with praise, with the declaration of God's mercy and power. He chose the atmosphere of his morning before the morning came. That is a spiritual discipline that will transform your life. If before you go to sleep tonight, you would say, "Lord, tomorrow morning when my eyes open, before I check my phone, before I look at the news, before I review my messages, before I rehearse my to-do list, I am going to open my mouth and bless your name. I am going to rehearse your goodness. I am going to count what you have done." That simple decision will reroute the entire trajectory of your day. Because here is what the enemy knows about mornings. He knows that the first frequency that occupies your mind in the morning sets the tone for the entire day. And so he works hard to make sure that the first thing you feel in the morning is the weight of what is unresolved. The first thought that occupies you is the problem that has no solution yet. He wants complain to be the morning frequency because he knows that a person who starts the day in complain will carry that frequency through every interaction, every prayer, every decision they make that day. But a person who starts the day in gratitude carries a different kind of light. They carry an atmosphere that the Holy Spirit can walk with throughout that day. Look at Psalm 59 again. Look at verse 16 and then compare it to verse one. the same crisis, the same danger, the same enemies. But by verse 16, David has come to a place of such settled confidence in God that the atmosphere of the psalm is completely different. That is what gratitude does. It does not change the external circumstances immediately, but it changes you. And when you change, you begin to engage the circumstances from a position of strength rather than a position of defeat. I want to speak now to someone who has been in what I would call the complain cycle. This is the place where you wake up, you complain, nothing changes. You go to sleep, you wake up again, you complain again, nothing changes. And the cycle goes on and on and you begin to lose hope not just about your situation but about God himself. You begin to wonder if he hears you. You begin to question whether your prayers are reaching the ceiling. You begin to feel spiritually dry, emotionally depleted, physically exhausted. And the complaint cycle is the engine driving all of that depletion. Because see what many people do not understand is that complaint is spiritually and emotionally exhausting. It depletes your faith. It empties your expectation. It distances you from the presence of God. Because God who inhabits praise does not come and sit in the midst of murmmory. He cannot. It is not that he does not want to. It is that the atmosphere of complaining is antithetical to his nature. He is the God of all glory. The God of abundance, the God of more than enough. And complaint is the language of scarcity, of lack, of insufficiency. These two atmospheres cannot coexist. But gratitude breaks the cycle. The moment you begin to give thanks genuinely, even if only for the small things, you shift the atmosphere. And when the atmosphere shifts, the presence of God moves in. And when the presence of God moves in, faith begins to rise. And when faith rises, expectation is renewed. And when expectation is renewed, you start to see things you were not seeing before. Doors you thought were closed begin to appear cracked open. Connections you thought were dead begin to come alive. Strategies and wisdom that had been blocked begin to flow. Because the God who inhabits praise is also the God who reveals secrets, who gives wisdom liberally, who opens rivers in the desert and makes a way where there is no way. Let me talk to you about another dimension of this. Romans 8:28 says, "We know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose." This is one of the most quoted verses in the Bible. But I want you to hear it through the lens of gratitude. Paul is saying that in the sovereign wisdom of God, every single thing, not some things, not most things, but all things are being woven together. They are being orchestrated by a God who sees the end from the beginning. Who sits outside of time. Who holds the entirety of your story in [music] his hands and who is working every thread, even the painful threads, even the ugly threads, even the threads that look like mistakes, into something that will ultimately serve his good purpose for your life. Gratitude is what the eye of faith looks like in practice. When you give thanks in the midst of a challenge, you are essentially saying, "God, I believe that you have not lost the plot of my story. I believe that this chapter, though painful, is not the final chapter. I believe that you are [music] weaving this into something that I cannot see yet from where I'm standing." That is not denial. That is not naivity. That is prophetic vision. That is the sight that comes to people who look at their circumstances through the lens of God's faithfulness rather than through the lens of their own limited understanding. Proverbs 3:5 and 6 says, "Trust in the Lord with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him and he shall direct your paths." Gratitude is the primary form of acknowledging God in your ways. When you wake up and say, "Lord, I thank you for this day," you are acknowledging that this day did not arrive by accident. When you eat a meal and pause to genuinely thank God, you are acknowledging that the provision is not primarily your own doing. When you arrive safely at your destination and you breathe a word of thanks, you are acknowledging the invisible hand that guarded your journey. Every act of genuine gratitude is an act of theological acknowledgement that God is in the details of your life. And that acknowledgment unlocks divine direction. You know what happens when you stop acknowledging God? When complaint replaces gratitude, you are essentially removing God from the equation of your daily life. You begin to process your circumstances from a purely natural perspective. You begin to make decisions driven by fear and frustration rather than by faith and divine wisdom. You begin to rely on your own analysis, your own strategies, your own strength. And beloved, I promise you, your own analysis, your own strategies, and your own strength are not enough for what you are facing. They were never designed to be enough. God built you to be a dependent creature. Not in the humiliating sense, but in the glorious sense that you were built to draw from a supply that is infinite, inexhaustible, and overflowing. And gratitude is the pipeline that keeps that supply flowing. Let me give you a prophetic picture. There is a well. This well is deep beyond measure. It water is clear. It is pure. It is healing. It is lifegiving. And every single person in this room, every single person reading and hearing this word has access to this well. But the well has a mechanism. It requires a particular kind of vessel to draw from it. And that vessel is made of praise and thanksgiving. Complaint cannot hold the water of this well. The moment you switch the vessel from gratitude to mmory, the water stops flowing. But when you switch back, when you pick up the vessel of thanksgiving, even with trembling hands, even with tears streaming down your face, even in the midnight of your crisis, the water [music] begins to flow again. I know someone right now who has been thirsty. I know someone who has been in a dry place, spiritually speaking, you have been praying, but the prayers feel flat. You have been reading the word, but the word feels distant. You have been going to church, but the services feel routine. You have been on the outside of a glory that you remember from before but cannot seem to access right now. [music] And I'm telling you prophetically, the issue is the vessel. Somewhere along the way, complaint [music] replaced thanksgiving in your daily rhythm and the flow was disrupted. But today, right now, in this moment, you can make the shift. You can pick up the vessel again. You can open your mouth and begin to bless the Lord. And I tell you, the water will flow. The presence will return. The fire will be rekindled. The joy [music] will come back. The strength will be renewed. Isaiah 40:31 says, "They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength. They shall mount up with wings as eagles. They shall run and not be weary. They shall walk and not faint." Waiting on the Lord is not a passive activity. In the Hebrew, it implies serving, attending, expectant posture. And you cannot genuinely wait on God in a posture of complaint. Complaining says I am tired of waiting. Gratitude says even in the waiting you are still God and I trust the timing of your faithfulness. Gratitude extends your capacity to wait. It keeps the flame of expectation alive in the long seasons of trust. Now I want to take you to the most powerful example of gratitude in the New Testament. And I want you to hold this story in your heart as we move toward the conclusion of this ministration. John chapter 11. Lazarus is dead. He has been dead for 4 days. The stone is rolled against the tomb. The mourers are weeping. The sisters Mary and Martha are heartbroken. Even the disciples are uncertain about what will happen next. And Jesus comes to the tomb and he gives an unusual command. He says, "Take away the stone." And before he speaks one word to the dead man, before he releases the resurrection command, before the miracle happens, the scripture says that Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, "Father, I thank thee that thou has heard me in the face of a 4-day old corpse. Before any visible sign of what was about to happen, Jesus released thanksgiving to the father." That is your pattern. Gratitude before the miracle, not after. Thanksgiving in advance, not only in retrospect because genuine spirit born gratitude operates in the realm of faith and faith calls things that be not as though they are. When you thank God for the breakthrough before the breakthrough comes, you are not being delusional. You are operating [music] in the same spirit that made Jesus say thank you while standing in front of a dead situation. And we know what happened next. He said Lazarus come forth and the dead man came out. Your dead situation is about to come out. Your dead marriage, your dead business, your dead vision, your dead relationship with God. As you shift from complaint to thanksgiving, as you begin to release gratitude in advance, as you begin to bless God for what he has already promised, even before the manifestation arrives, things that have been dead in your life are going to hear the voice of the Lord and begin to come forth. I said they are going to come forth. Let me tell you something else about gratitude. It is contagious. When you cultivate a lifestyle of gratitude, you become a carrier of a spiritual atmosphere that affects everyone around you. People in your home begin to breathe easier. People in your workplace begin to feel lighter in your presence. You become a source of encouragement, a wellspring of hope, an anchor in the storm for the people who encounter you. This is what it means to be the light of the world and the salt of the earth. Not just to preach at people, but to carry a quality of inner life, a depth of gratitude and joy that makes people want to know the God that you know. The Apostle Paul in Colossians 3:15 says, "Let the peace of God rule in your hearts to the which also ye are called in one body, and be ye thankful." And then in verse 16, he says, "Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord." He connects thankfulness to the dwelling of the word of Christ and the dwelling of the word of Christ to the richness of community and the richness of community to songs and psalms and spiritual worship. It is all connected. Gratitude is the thread that weaves the tapestry of a spiritfilled life together. Now, as we approach the moment of prayer, I want to give you a practical charge from today. I want you to create what I call a gratitude altar in your heart and in your home. An altar is a place of deliberate encounter. [music] An altar is not accidental. An altar is built. And I want you to build an altar of gratitude in your life. Every morning before you check your messages, before you review your challenges, spend at least 5 minutes and deliberately name what God has done. Name the specific things, not vague things. Specific things. Name the morning. Name the breath. Name the person who stayed. Name the provision that came. Name the time God showed up when you had no other recourse. Name it out loud because there is power in the spoken declaration of gratitude. And throughout the day, I want you to practice what I call gratitude interruptions. These are moments where you consciously interrupt the flow of complaint, of anxiety, of worry, and replace that flow with a deliberate acknowledgment of God's goodness. It does not have to be long. It does not have to be elaborate. It can be as simple as, "Lord, thank you." Just, "Lord, thank you." Because those three words released from a sincere heart, carry enough spiritual weight to shift an atmosphere, to break a stronghold, to invite the presence of God into an ordinary Tuesday afternoon. I want to add something before we pray because the Holy Spirit is pressing this into me right now. Someone in this space, someone receiving this word has been dealing with a spirit of ingratitude that goes beyond personality or circumstance. It has a name and it has been assigned against you because ingratitude and complaint are not just bad habits for some people. They are spirits. They attach themselves to bloodlines. They attach themselves to people who have carried wounds for a long time. Who have been disappointed by God or who think they have been disappointed by God. Who have prayed and felt that the prayer was not answered. Who have believed and felt that the belief was not honored. Who have trusted and felt that the trust was betrayed. And out of that place of heart, a spirit of ingratitude crept in. And now it colors everything. Even when good things happen, it minimizes them. Even when God shows up, it finds a reason to question his motives. Even when the blessing is evident, he says, "Yes, but I am breaking that spirit today in the name of Jesus by the authority of the word of God. I am breaking that assignment off of your life right now. And I am inviting the spirit of the Lord to come and fill every space, that spirit occupied with genuine, deep, overflowing, spirit-born gratitude. I am inviting the river of thanksgiving to begin to flow through your life again. I am inviting the joy of the Lord which is your strength to come and reoccupy the spaces that grief and bitterness had taken. And before we go into prayer, please share this message. Share it with someone who needs to hear it. Share it with someone who has been in the complaint cycle. Share it with someone whose life has been colored by ingratitude without them knowing it. Share it because this word is a seed. and seeds need to be swn broadly to produce a harvest. Share it and watch what God does on both sides of the sharing. When you share it, the anointing on the word does not diminish, it multiplies. So please right now share this word before we go into prayer and let us release it as an act of faith believing that it will touch the hearts that need it most. Now lift your hands. Lift your hands wherever you are. right there in your room, in your car, at your desk, wherever you are receiving this word, lift your hands to the father. Let us go into prayer. Father, in the name of Jesus, we come before you right now. We come not because we have it all together. We come not because every situation is resolved. We come not because the pressure has lifted. We come because you are God. And we have made the decision today that regardless of what we are facing, regardless of what we are feeling, regardless of what the circumstances say, we will open our mouths and we will bless your name. Lord, we thank you. We thank you for life. For the simple, profound, irreplaceable gift of life. For the fact that our eyes open this morning. For the fact that our minds are functioning. For the fact that breath is [music] moving through these lungs. Lord, a million people who had plans yesterday did not wake up to see today. But we did and we will not take that lightly. We will not treat that grace cheaply. We open our mouths and we say, "Thank you, God. Thank you." We thank you for the blood of Jesus Christ that washes us clean. We thank you for the finished work of Calvary that took every sin, every shame, every guilt, every condemnation, and nailed it to the cross. We thank you that we stand before you today not by our own righteousness but by the righteousness of your son who took our place. What a substitute. What a sacrifice. What an unspeakable gift. Lord, we bless you for Calvary. We thank you for the Holy Spirit who lives inside us. Not just around us, not just with us, but inside us. The third person of the Godhead has taken up residence in these earthn vessels. And Lord, that alone makes our lives extraordinary. We are not ordinary people. We carry an extraordinary guest. We thank you Holy Spirit for your presence. We thank you for your comfort. We thank you for your counsel. We thank you for the way you intercede for us when we do not even know how to pray. We thank you Holy Spirit. We bless you right now. Now, Father, I come against every spirit of ingratitude in the name of Jesus. Every assignment of the enemy that has been using complaint and murmmoring to drain the faith of your people, I command that assignment to be dismantled right now. By the authority of the name above every name, by the power of the blood that was shed on Calvary, [music] I break every chain of ingratitude. I break every stronghold of complaint. I break every spirit of discouragement that has been using the language of murmuring to hold God's people in cycles of defeat in the name of Jesus. I lose every person receiving this word from the prison of complaint. I lose them from the cycle of rehearsing problems. I lose them from the habit of ingratitude that has been blocking the flow of God's goodness in their lives. I release them into a new era of thanksgiving, of praise, of gratitude foiled faith. Spirit of God, come now and do the deep work. Reach into the chambers of every heart that has been wounded. Reach into the places where disappointment stored itself. Reach into the rooms where unfulfilled expectations turned into bitterness and resentment. Reach into those dark places and release the healing river of your grace. Let [music] your presence flood every wound. Let your love speak to every hurt. Let your word minister to every broken expectation and let thankfulness arise like the sun out of those healed places. Let gratitude rise. [music] I prophesy over every person receiving this word right now. I speak to your morning. I speak to your tomorrow morning and the morning after that. I declare that from this day forward, your mornings will begin differently. Your mouth will open and blessing will come out before complaint finds its way in. You are entering a season of morning praise. You are entering a season where your first language of the day will be the language of heaven, the language of gratitude, the language of faith. I prophesy that as you shift your posture from complain to thanksgiving, situations that have been stuck for months, for years are going to begin to move. The God who inhabits praise is going to show up in the middle of your situation and begin to rearrange things. Doors that were closed are going to open. Connections that seem dead are going to come alive. resources that seemed impossible are going to begin to flow because when God sits down in the midst of your praise, [music] the kingdom of God begins to manifest in the space where complaint used to live. I break the word of Deuteronomy 28:47 over your life. That scripture says, "Because thou servest not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things, the consequences came. I break the spirit of joyless service. I break the pattern of serving God reluctantly, of worshiping God mechanically, of praying God listly. I declare that a new fire of joyful gratitude is igniting in your spirit right now. You are going to worship differently from this day forward. You are going to pray differently. You are [music] going to approach God with a fresh awareness of his goodness and a renewed fire of thanksgiving. Father, for the person who has been holding on to a complaint against you, for the person who has been quietly angry at God for something that happened, for a prayer that seemed unanswered, for a season that was painful, for a loss that made no sense, for a closed door that they do not understand. Lord, I bring that person before you right now. You know who they are. You know the specific wound. You know the specific night that [music] broke something in their heart toward you. Lord, I ask you to speak to them now. Let your love meet them in the place of that wound. Let your peace stand where confusion has stood. Let your understanding which passes all human reasoning come and satisfy the deepest questions of their heart. And let them come back to you not just as a servant but as a worshipper. Let them come back with thanksgiving. Let them come back with praise. For the family that has been divided by a spirit of complaint, where the atmosphere in the home has been toxic, where mornings begin with irritation and evenings end with exhaustion, where no one is grateful and [music] everyone is taking everyone else for granted. I release the spirit of thanksgiving into that home right now. I declare that the atmosphere of that home is changing. I declare that gratitude is being restored between spouses, between parents and children, between siblings. I declare that the language of appreciation and acknowledgement is coming back into those homes. What the enemy meant to divide through complaint, God is going to use gratitude to reunite. Lord, for the businesses, for the careers, for the finances, Father, I declare that every child of God who receives this word and makes the shift from complaint to gratitude is entering a new season of supernatural provision. For the scripture says that a grateful heart is a magnet for divine multiplication. Lord, multiply the seeds that have been swn by faithful people who have chosen to trust you even in the difficult seasons. Let the harvest come. Let the overflow come. Let the abundance that you promise come now in the name of Jesus. I command depression to flee. I command anxiety to dissolve. I command fear to lose its grip. I command hopelessness to pack its bags [music] and vacate the premises. Because a person who has entered into genuine gratitude cannot be held by depression. Gratitude and depression cannot coexist in the same heart. Light and darkness cannot occupy the same space. As gratitude comes in, the darkness has to leave. And I declare that darkness is leaving right now. I speak to physical bodies. Bodies that have been under attack. Bodies that have been carrying the weight of stress and anxiety, which we know now even medically produces physical [music] disease. I declare that the atmosphere of gratitude that is entering your life is [music] also a healing atmosphere for your body. For there is research now confirming what the word of God has always known that a merry heart doeth good like a medicine. I declare healing into bodies, healing into immune systems, healing into nervous systems that have been frayed by years of anxiety and complaints. Let the medicine of gratitude and the joy of the Lord begin to produce physical wholeness in these bodies in Jesus name. Lord I ask that the hunger for your presence would intensify in every person who hears this word. Let a holy dissatisfaction with superficial Christianity arise. Let a longing for deeper encounter with you, deeper communion, deeper worship arise out of this season of cultivated gratitude. For it is the grateful heart that pursues the giver more than the gifts. It is a thankful spirit that says, "Lord, I am not just looking for what you can do. I am looking for you. I am grateful not just for the blessings but for the blesser. Not just for the provisions but for the provider. Not just for the miracles but for the miracle working God. Let that kind of gratitude arise. Let that quality of seeking be restored. Father, I thank you for this word today. I thank you for every heart that received it. I thank you for the shift that is happening right now in this moment in spirits and souls and bodies across every location where this word is being received.
